title: IIM Ahmedabad Gold Medallist Shubham Goyal Leads a 13-Member Team at Microsoft
excerpt: The IIM-A graduate — Institute Rank 1 in his first year among 393 students, with the best overall GPA in the institute's MBA history — now leads a 13-member team at the software giant after patenting AI product work as a project lead.
body:
• Shubham Goyal, a gold medallist from the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad, now leads a 13-member team at Microsoft, according to a profile published by India Today on Tuesday.
  • At IIMA he secured Institute Rank 1 in his first year — in a batch of 393 students — earning the Desh Ratna Dr. Rajendra Prasad Gold Medal for scholastic performance.
  • His LinkedIn profile records an overall graduating GPA of 4.00/4.33, which he states is the best overall GPA in the institute's MBA batch history since its founding in 1961.
  • At Microsoft he has served as project lead on patented AI work, including an AI-based video summary generation system and a Copilot feature that converts multimedia content into visual diagrams.

An IIM Ahmedabad gold medallist now leads a 13-member team at Microsoft, capping an academic record that stands among the finest the institute has produced. Shubham Goyal, whose performance at IIMA included Institute Rank 1 in his first year and the best overall GPA in the institute's MBA history, was profiled by India Today on Tuesday as the leader of a 13-person team at the software giant.

Goyal's trajectory was set in the classroom. His LinkedIn profile records that he topped his first year of the IIMA MBA — a batch of 393 students — to win the Desh Ratna Dr. Rajendra Prasad Gold Medal for scholastic performance. He lists an overall graduating GPA of 4.00/4.33, which he states is the best overall GPA in an IIMA MBA batch since the institute's inception in 1961, a claim he says was verified by the manager of IIMA's MBA programme.

"I had an Overall GPA of 4.00/4.33 which is the Best Overall GPA in an IIMA MBA batch till date (since its inception in 1961)."

— Shubham Goyal, in his LinkedIn profile

From the classroom to Copilot

Goyal was among the scholastic medal recipients at IIM Ahmedabad's 57th annual convocation in April 2022, where 584 students graduated across the institute's programmes. The convocation address was delivered by Falguni Nayar, founder and CEO of Nykaa and an IIMA alumna, alongside Kumar Mangalam Birla, chairperson of the institute's board of governors, and director Errol D'Souza. Nayar urged the graduating class to take bold bets early: "Don't be afraid to take risks along the way," she said, advising them to spend their early careers "taking the right risks and making some bold bets on yourself."

At Microsoft, Goyal has worked at the sharp end of the company's AI push. His profile lists two Microsoft patents granted with him as project lead: an "AI-based video summary generation for visual consumption" system, with the patent filed on October 23, 2024 and a $750 cash award, and a "Copilot Transform to diagram" feature that converts multimedia content into visual diagrams, which carried a $450 award.

Why this story resonates with the diaspora

Indians are increasingly visible in leadership and engineering roles at the world's largest technology firms, and the arc from an Indian classroom to a product team in Redmond is one the diaspora knows well. Microsoft has also deepened its India bet in parallel: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal recently met Microsoft India president Puneet Chandok to discuss expanding data-centre capacity and advancing the India AI Mission, following Microsoft's plan to invest $17.5 billion in India over four years in cloud and AI infrastructure. Engineers educated at Indian institutes who go on to lead AI product work at these firms are, increasingly, the story of the AI era.

What to watch

Whether Goyal's patented video-summarization and Copilot diagram work makes its way into shipped Microsoft products — and what an Indian-educated product leader does next at a company pouring billions into AI infrastructure in India. Profiles like his also function as signals to recruiters and aspirants alike: IIM Ahmedabad's placement machinery continues to place its graduates at the top of global technology firms, and academic records like a 4.00 GPA remain rare currency even in an industry that claims to have moved past credentials.
